items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to receive claimed refund
items.quote: Damit wir sie auszahlen können, überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date in the text itself: 'bis zum 27.11.2026'. No period to count and no deemed-delivery calculation is needed since the date is printed as written. 27.11.2026 is a Friday, a normal business day in NW, so no weekend/holiday shift applies.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: it demands an upfront 'Bearbeitungsgebühr' before releasing a much larger promised 'refund', a pattern used by fraudulent 'Rückerstattungsstelle'-sounding operations that are not real German consumer-protection bodies.

The payment IBAN (CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600) is a Cyprus account; a genuine German energy-cost refund or an official German consumer body would not require a fee to be sent to a foreign private account, and this IBAN only passes basic format/checksum checks — it proves nothing about who actually owns the account.

The sender's address is in Nikosia, Zypern (Cyprus), with only a Cyprus phone number and a generic example.com-style email address; there is no identifiable German energy supplier, grid operator or regulator behind this claim.

The letter uses urgency and an irreversible-loss threat ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig.') to pressure quick payment, a classic scam technique, and gives no breakdown of which specific energy contract or supplier the alleged 2023-2025 overpayment relates to.

There is no Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung and no real legal basis cited for either the claimed refund or the fee; do not transfer any money or reply with personal/bank details — verify independently with your actual energy supplier or the official Verbraucherzentrale before taking any action, and consider reporting this letter as a likely scam.
